source_evidence: Typically, you pay a broker a fee called a commission or markup every time you buy or sell an investment.  Typically you pay an adviser an ongoing asset-based fee based on the total value of your account.
question: Misconception: A transaction-based fee is based on the total value of your account, while an asset-based fee is charged every time you buy or sell an investment.
answer: Correction: The source describes the reverse. A broker typically charges a commission or markup each time you buy or sell; an adviser typically charges an ongoing asset-based fee based on your account’s total value.
